newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Lag in banks passing on rate cuts widens - RBA.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Lag in banks passing on rate cuts widens - RBA.

text.p: Australian banks had increased the lag between reducing interest rates following the 1996 rate cuts compared to the time it took to pass on increases following 1994 rate rises, the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) said on Tuesday.

"This is particularly the case for existing housing loans, where the average lag in 1996 between the time of monetary policy announcements and the reductions in housing loan rates becoming effective was around six to seven weeks, compared with about two weeks when banks raised rates in 1994," the RBA said in its February Bulletin.
This lag was also much longer than for new borrowers, who received reduced rates within a week of the official rate cuts.
"The implementation lags for new and existing small business borrowers (around five to six weeks) and large business (around three to four weeks) were also longer than lags in 1994," the RBA said.
